items.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: But also things like Peggy Lee and Ray Conniff and all that.

ctx.x: But also things like Peggy Lee and Ray Conniff and all that. But what did you hear in your house?

Well again, my dad had a humungous record collection that we listened to constantly and I heard anything from the swing era bands to early Dixieland bands and Eddie Condon style. And actually it was very funny because when my brother and I went through our adolescent rebellion in our early pre-teens and teens, our rebellion against our father was buying Miles Davis records and Charlie Parker records, which he didn’t care for because that was the music that they ruined after he came back from World War II.
